title: Role of the Transport Supports
learningObjectives: State the structural role of the transport supports.
student: State the role of the two transport supports.
instructor: The supports transfer the column self-weight to the trailer while controlling bending demand in the transported member.

title: Dominant External Loading
learningObjectives: Identify the dominant load in the simplified model.
student: Identify the dominant external load acting on the column in the simplified transport model.
instructor: The column self-weight is represented by a uniform distributed load w over the full length L.

title: Support Boundary Conditions
learningObjectives: Describe the support idealizations and admitted reactions.
student: How should the two transport supports be idealized, and which reactions do they provide?
instructor: Model them as simple point supports that permit rotation and provide upward vertical reactions but no reaction moments.

title: Load Path to the Road
learningObjectives: Trace the column load to the road surface.
student: Trace the load path from the column to the road.
instructor: Column self-weight transfers through the transport blocks to the trailer bed and frame, then through the suspension and axles to the road surface.

title: Expected Critical Moment Locations
learningObjectives: Anticipate the locations of positive and negative moment extrema.
student: Before calculating, where should the governing positive and negative bending moments be expected?
instructor: Negative moments occur at the two supports because of the overhangs. By symmetry, the maximum positive moment occurs at the beam center.

title: Symmetric Support Arrangement
learningObjectives: Justify equal offsets using geometry and loading symmetry.
student: Why is it reasonable to place the supports at equal offsets from the two ends?
instructor: The uniform column geometry and distributed loading are symmetric, so the optimal idealized static support arrangement is also symmetric.

title: Support-Placement Tradeoff
learningObjectives: Explain the competing effects controlled by support location.
student: Explain why placing the supports either too close to the ends or too close to the center is unfavorable.
instructor: Supports near the ends leave a long interior span and produce a large positive center moment. Supports near the center create long overhangs and large negative support moments.

title: Student-Generated Beam Idealization
learningObjectives: Translate the transport system into a beam model and FBD.
student: Before viewing the reference figure, draw a beam of total length L carrying uniform load w. Place supports at x = a and x = L - a, and label the equal overhangs and reactions.
instructor: A valid FBD shows a uniformly loaded beam from x = 0 to x = L, upward reactions R1 and R2 at the two supports, and equal end overhangs a.
gradingNotes: Students should create their model before seeing the instructor reference idealization.

title: Modeling Assumptions
learningObjectives: State assumptions defining the model's scope.
student: State the assumptions used to represent the transport condition.
instructor: Assume a straight, uniform, prismatic column; uniformly distributed self-weight; static loading; point supports; continuous contact with both supports; and small deformation. Neglect road dynamics, tie-down forces, local bearing stress, and cracking.

title: Optimization Analysis Plan
learningObjectives: Plan the mechanics and optimization sequence.
student: List the calculation sequence needed to find the optimal support offset.
instructor: Use symmetry and equilibrium to find the reactions; derive piecewise shear and moment functions; identify the negative support and positive center moments; equate their magnitudes; solve for a/L; and construct the optimized diagrams.

title: Support Locations and Reactions
learningObjectives: Identify support coordinates and reaction directions.
student: Identify the support locations and reaction directions using coordinate x measured from the left end.
instructor: The supports are at x = a and x = L - a. Each provides an upward vertical reaction.

title: Support Reactions
learningObjectives: Determine reactions using symmetry and equilibrium.
student: Use symmetry and vertical equilibrium to determine R1 and R2.
instructor: The total distributed load is wL. Therefore R1 = R2 = wL/2 = {{column_reaction_kip}} kip. The total column weight is {{column_total_weight_kip}} kip.

title: Piecewise Beam Regions
learningObjectives: Partition the beam for internal-resultant equations.
student: Divide the column into the three regions required for piecewise shear and moment analysis.
instructor: Region I: 0 ≤ x < a; Region II: a ≤ x ≤ L - a; Region III: L - a < x ≤ L.

title: Piecewise Shear Functions
learningObjectives: Derive shear force in all beam regions.
student: Using upward force as positive, derive V(x) in each region.
instructor: Region I: V = -wx. Region II: V = wL/2 - wx. Region III: V = wL - wx.

title: Piecewise Bending-Moment Functions
learningObjectives: Derive bending moment in all beam regions.
student: Derive M(x) in each region using M(0) = 0.
instructor:
Region I: M = -wx2/2.

Region II: M = -wx2/2 + (wL/2)(x - a).

Region III: M = -wx2/2 + (wL/2)(x - a) + (wL/2)[x - (L - a)].

title: Negative Support Moment
learningObjectives: Calculate the negative moment at either support.
student: Determine the bending moment at either support.
instructor: Ms = -wa2/2. At the optimal offset, Ms = {{column_support_moment_kipft}} kip·ft.

title: Positive Center Moment
learningObjectives: Calculate the positive moment at beam center.
student: Determine the positive bending moment at x = L/2.
instructor: Mc = wL2/8 - wLa/2. At the optimal offset, Mc = {{column_center_moment_kipft}} kip·ft.

title: Minimax Condition
learningObjectives: Formulate the minimax support-placement condition.
student: Apply a minimax argument by making the governing positive and negative moment magnitudes equal.
instructor: Set |Ms| = Mc: wa2/2 = wL2/8 - wLa/2. Canceling w gives a2 + La - L2/4 = 0.

title: Optimal Support Offset
learningObjectives: Solve for the optimal dimensionless support offset.
student: Solve the minimax equation and report a as a fraction of L and as a numerical value for the assigned column.
instructor: The physically admissible root is a = [(√2 - 1)/2]L = {{column_optimal_ratio}}L. For L = {{column_L}} {{column_L_unit}}, a = {{column_optimal_offset_ft}} ft. The support spacing is {{column_support_spacing_ft}} ft.

title: Minimized Maximum Moment
learningObjectives: Calculate the minimized absolute maximum bending moment.
student: Determine the minimized absolute maximum bending moment.
instructor: |M|max = [ (3 - 2√2)/8 ]wL2 = {{column_moment_coefficient}}wL2 = {{column_max_abs_moment_kipft}} kip·ft.

title: Optimized Shear and Moment Diagrams
learningObjectives: Construct and label optimized internal-resultant diagrams.
student: Draw the optimized shear-force and bending-moment diagrams. Label the values at both ends, immediately before and after each support, and at the center.
instructor:
Shear values from left to right are: end {{column_V_left_kip}} kip; left support minus {{column_V_left_support_minus_kip}} kip; left support plus {{column_V_left_support_plus_kip}} kip; center {{column_V_center_kip}} kip; right support minus {{column_V_right_support_minus_kip}} kip; right support plus {{column_V_right_support_plus_kip}} kip; right end {{column_V_right_kip}} kip.

The moment diagram is quadratic and continuous: zero at both free ends, {{column_support_moment_kipft}} kip·ft at each support, and {{column_center_moment_kipft}} kip·ft at center.

title: Engineering Recommendation and Limits
learningObjectives: Communicate a support-placement recommendation with appropriate limits.
student: Give a concise support-placement recommendation and state at least one important limitation of the model.
instructor: {{column_recommendation}}
gradingNotes: A complete recommendation should include the offset from each end and at least one omitted real-system effect.
commonMistakes: Do not recommend the center-to-center support spacing as though it were the end offset.
